Verified on candidate sha256:aa219bd2 (repair T-DG6-BE-Z1). (1) exports-assembly 0125 guard test: BE-Z1 adds, after the refused UPDATE, a blocking 'SELECT id FROM export_job WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE', which waits on the aborting transaction's row lock (PostgreSQL sends the ErrorResponse before AbortCurrentTransaction releases it) instead of a timer. My round-2 probe method, re-written on the candidate's file copied verbatim (zz-qa-dg6r3-assembly-guard-lock.test.ts), 80 repetitions per variant on a disposable PostgreSQL at load ~16: 'fixed' (the candidate's sequence) 0 misses of 80; 'mutant' (the same sequence without the FOR UPDATE line, i.e. the round-2 test) 11 misses of 80, each leaving the job queued, snapshot null, version 1, attempts 0 (10-f200-probe-assembly-guard-lock.log; exit 1 BY DESIGN: only the mutant variant's assertion fails). (2) change-requests-in-tx: auditXmin now orders by occurred_at, seq (seq is the audit_event identity column, migration 0003). The candidate file passes alone 3 of 3 (6/6 tests each); a mutant ordering DESC fails exactly test (a) '...round-2 resubmission...' (10b-f200-probe-xmin-order.log), so the test depends on the order the repair fixes. (3) Both files pass in integration run 1 (half B: exports-assembly 18/18, change-requests-in-tx 6/6); run 2 is reported in the record.
